Background Disorders of mental health are known to affect cognitive functions, hence called as cognitive disorders. Impaired glucose metabolism, insulin resistance, vitamin-D deficiency and oxidative stress are some of the key early events reported to be involved in the pathogenesis of most common cognitive disorders, which include Alzheimer’s disease. Type-2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is one of the known contributing factors of cognitive impairment and dementia. Methods A cross sectional study was carried out in 145 subjects, who were assessed for cognitive function by modified mini mental status examination (3MS). In addition, measurement of fasting blood sugar (FBS), fasting insulin, HbA1c, lipid profile, vitamin D and oxidative markers was performed. Participants were divided into different groups based on (a) vitamin D insufficiency and sufficiency; (b) diabetic and non-diabetic with and without cognitive impairment. Results The study included a total of 145 subjects; 51 males and 94 females and the mean age was 68.24±9.70 years. Among diabetics with vitamin D insufficiency, 35 subjects (71.43%) had cognitive impairment, but, among non-diabetics with vitamin D insufficiency, 27 subjects (62.79%) had cognitive impairment. Chi square test showed no significant association between diabetes, vitamin D insufficiency and cognitive impairment. Glutathione peroxidase (GPx) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) levels were non-significantly lower in cognition-impaired subjects, when compared to cognition normal subjects in diabetics with vitamin D insufficiency. Conclusion Our study showed that cognitive impairment is more predominant in individuals with diabetes. However, our study did not find any significant relationship between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress. A significant association was found only with GPx and 3MSE score in vitamin D insufficient non-diabetics. molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.activity_type_context: Cognitive disorders (including Alzheimer 9s disease, cognitive impairment, and dementia), Type-2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), serum vitamin D deficiency, and oxidative stress (OS) are key contexts. Vitamin D also exhibits neuroprotective, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory functions.
molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.mechanism_description: Impaired glucose metabolism, insulin resistance, vitamin-D deficiency, and oxidative stress are early events in the pathogenesis of cognitive disorders, including Alzheimer 9s disease (AD). AD is characterized by amyloid beta (A 2) peptide accumulation and neurofibrillary tangles, alongside impaired glucose metabolism, insulin resistance, altered insulin signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction, and oxidative stress. Vitamin D stimulates amyloid plaque clearance, reduces amyloid-induced cytotoxicity, apoptosis, and inflammation. 25-dihydroxyvitamin D inhibits pro-inflammatory cytokines (e.g., TNF- 1), regulates NF- 2B, and suppresses TLR-2/-4, thereby reducing insulin resistance and diabetes risk. Insulin resistance and oxidative stress are common factors in T2DM and vitamin D deficiency, leading to cognitive dysfunction. Oxidative stress, resulting from an imbalance in ROS production and removal, contributes to AD pathogenesis, insulin resistance, and diabetic complications. Vitamin D receptors in the central nervous system influence neurogenesis, calcium signaling, neurotrophic factor expression, amyloid-beta clearance, and prevent neurodegeneration. Vitamin D also acts as an antioxidant by inhibiting free radical formation and modulates pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines (e.g., TNF- 1, IL-6, IL-12) from peripheral mononuclear cells, which can induce CNS neuro-inflammation and cognitive dysfunction.

dose_intensity_and_specificity.dose_comparison_summary: The study compared subjects based on vitamin D insufficiency and sufficiency, as well as diabetic vs. non-diabetic status. Among diabetics with vitamin D insufficiency, 71.43% experienced cognitive impairment, compared to 62.79% among non-diabetics with vitamin D insufficiency. A 7-year follow-up study noted a strong association between elevated vitamin D intake and a lower risk of developing AD in older women. While comparisons were made between diabetic and non-diabetic groups (based on HbA1c), no dose-response effect of vitamin D therapy was observed in this study. Furthermore, previous studies cited found no significant differences in cognitive outcomes between high-dose vs. low-dose vitamin D therapy in T2DM patients, nor significant improvements with vitamin D supplementation vs. placebo in young adults.
dose_intensity_and_specificity.specificity_finding: Overall, no significant association was found between diabetes, vitamin D insufficiency, and cognitive impairment. However, a significant association was specifically identified between Glutathione peroxidase (GPx) and 3MSE score in vitamin D insufficient non-diabetics. It was also noted that anti-oxidative parameters in peripheral circulation (like SOD, GPx, and total anti-oxidative activity of serum) are likely not accurate reflections of oxidative stress conditions in the brain.

clinical_implication_and_population.target_population: The study focused on elderly patients with and without Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) with a mean age of 68.24 19.70 years (51 males, 94 females), drawn from a larger population of 145 participants aged 43 190 years from an outpatient department. This included Indians above 60 years affected by dementia, elderly people affected by AD, older women in vitamin D intake studies, and individuals with and without vitamin D insufficiency/sufficiency experiencing cognitive impairment. Other referenced populations include older adults with mild cognitive impairment and young adults.
clinical_implication_and_population.health_implication: Cognitive impairment is more predominant in individuals with diabetes, as T2DM is a known contributing factor to cognitive impairment and dementia. Cognitive disorders are increasing globally. Lower 25(OH)D levels are associated with an increased risk of cognitive impairment. Conversely, elevated vitamin D intake is linked to a lower risk of developing AD and can mitigate insulin resistance and T2DM. Lower 3MS scores consistently indicate cognitive impairment across various diabetic and vitamin D status groups. Higher GPx and FBS levels negatively correlate with 3MS scores in vitamin D insufficient non-diabetics, suggesting a link to worse cognitive function.
clinical_implication_and_population.risk_classification: Individuals with T2DM and lower 25(OH)D levels face an increased or adverse risk of cognitive impairment and dementia. Elevated vitamin D intake is associated with a protective benefit against AD risk. The 3MS score holds diagnostic utility for identifying cognitive impairment. Diabetes is considered a risk factor for cognitive impairment, and higher GPx and FBS levels serve as risk markers associated with worse cognition in specific non-diabetic groups.

biomarker_reliability_and_future_focus.reliability_assessment: The study broadly found no significant relationship between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress. Although Glutathione peroxidase (GPx) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) levels were non-significantly lower in cognition-impaired diabetics with vitamin D insufficiency, a significant association was specifically noted between GPx and 3MSE score in vitamin D insufficient non-diabetics. The modified mini mental status (3MS) test is considered a widely used and validated neuropsychological test for assessing cognitive function and screening for dementia. However, peripheral anti-oxidative parameters (such as SOD, GPx, and total anti-oxidative activity of serum) are considered poor indicators for reflecting oxidative stress conditions in the brain.
recommended_alternatives: Inflammatory markers (e.g., TNF- 1, IL-6, IL-12) to investigate their role in CNS neuro-inflammation and cognitive dysfunction.
